description.value: A dimensional principal component analysis identified components of apathy and impulsivity, and voxel-based morphometry examined their grey- and white-matter correlates across frontotemporal lobar degeneration syndromes.

value: apathy and impulsivity are multifactorial constructs, but with common and overlapping features
subjective and objective measures relate to the same components
distinct frontostriatal, frontotemporal and brainstem circuits support the components of apathy and impulsivity

spans.text: Our specific hypotheses were that (i) apathy and impulsivity are multifactorial constructs, but with common and overlapping features; (ii) subjective and objective measures relate to the same components; and (iii) distinct frontostriatal, frontotemporal and brainstem circuits support the components of apathy and impulsivity.

Component 1

source_definition.value: Principal Component 1, patient-rated change: increased questionnaire endorsement of apathy, impulsivity, depression, anhedonia, and low motivation.

spans.text: Component 1 reflects patient ratings on questionnaires of apathy, impulsivity and related changes termed ‘Patient-rated change’.
Component 2

source_definition.value: Principal Component 2, carer-rated change in everyday skills and self-care, weighted to carer AES, CBI everyday skills, self-care, sleep and motivation, and NPI apathy.

spans.text: Component 2, termed ‘Carer-rated change in everyday skills and self-care’, is weighted to carer AES, Cambridge Behavioural Inventory (CBI) (everyday skills, self-care, sleep and motivation) and the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI) apathy subscore.
Component 3

source_definition.value: Principal Component 3, carer-rated change in complex behaviours, weighted to carer AES, CBI abnormal behaviour, eating habits and stereotypic behaviours, and NPI disinhibition.

spans.text: The carer AES also loads onto Component 3 ‘Carer-rated change in complex behaviours’, in addition to remaining subscores of the CBI (abnormal behaviour, eating habits, stereotypic behaviours) and the NPI-disinhibition.
Component 4

source_definition.value: Principal Component 4, impulsive behaviours, reflecting poor performance on NoGo, information sampling, and cued reinforcement tasks.

spans.text: Component 4 is associated with poor performance on NoGo, information sampling and cued reinforcement tasks, and termed ‘Impulsive behaviours’.
Component 7

source_definition.value: Principal Component 7, SST performance, with higher scores reflecting shorter stop-signal reaction times.

spans.text: On Component 7, termed ‘SST performance’, high scores reflect shorter stop-signal reaction times.

model_settings.value: Voxel-based morphometry general linear model using smoothed normalized grey- and white-matter segments; design matrix included eight mean-centred PCA factor scores, age, gender, total intracranial volume, and an intercept. Positive and negative contrasts were tested. Cluster-level family-wise-error correction used P<0.05 with an uncorrected voxel height threshold of P<0.005; non-stationary cluster-extent correction was applied.

spans.text: The design matrix included the eight mean centred Principal Component Factor scores, age, gender and total intracranial volume and an intercept. Both positive and negative contrasts were examined from the General Linear Model for all eight principal components.
